newsitem.title: USA: Irish envoy hails Clinton's role in Irish peace process.
newsitem.headline: Irish envoy hails Clinton's role in Irish peace process.

text.p: President Bill Clinton's role in the Irish peace process was described this week as critically important to secure peace.

"It was undeniably the courage and commitment of one man, President Clinton, which helped to secure the prize of peace for 17 months in Northern Ireland," said Irish ambassador Dermot Gallagher at the launch of a book on Tuesday night about Clinton's involvement in the issue.
Clinton's role in helping to secure the 1994 IRA ceasefire is detailed in the book "Daring Diplomacy" by Irish Times journalist Conor O'Clery.
"That commitment will again, I believe, be of critical importance in the coming period," Gallagher added.

Peace talks in Northen Ireland, chaired by Clinton's envoy, former Sen. George Mitchell, have adjourned until after the British general election, expected in May. Sinn Fein, the IRA's political wing, has been excluded from the talks until the IRA restores a ceasefire that broke down a year ago, after 17 months.
